body:
You are drafting dialogue for "Curse of Strahd", a single-player D&D 5e (2024 rules) computer game set in Barovia. I need about 30 lines for ONE group of scenes in this message (a second message will ask for the next group). Reply with plain text only: the lines under the node names given below, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The situation

Ireena Kolyana is a tall red-haired woman in her early twenties, the adopted daughter of the late burgomaster of the village of Barovia. The vampire lord Strahd hunts her. The player's party has left her to shelter in the town of Vallaki, either at the Blue Water Inn or in St. Andral's church, and has gone about its business.

Izek Strazni is the Baron's enforcer in Vallaki: a big scarred man in a watch captain's coat whose right arm is not his own (scaled red-black to the shoulder, clawed, hot, and able to burst into flame). When he was nine, wolves took his little sister in the woods by the lake, and took his arm too. He has dreamed of a red-haired woman every night since and pays the toymaker to carve dolls of her face. He has seen Ireena. Neither of them knows she is his lost sister, and he does not know it either; he only knows he wants her, safe, near him, never in the woods again.

A visit now comes to the party, at night, while the party is somewhere in Vallaki (the inn, the church, or the town square): somebody local brings them news about Izek and Ireena. There are three stages, each its own scene, played at different nights:

1. OMEN. Izek has taken to standing, motionless, outside the place where Ireena sleeps, staring at her window. Nothing has happened yet. A warning.
2. TAKEN. Some nights later, during the small hours, Izek walked in (the inn) or through the churchyard (the church) and carried her off to his room in the Baron's mansion. He did not hurt her; she is unhurt as far as anyone knows. Nobody stopped him. She is in his room, off the great hall. The door is not locked. He sits in front of it.
3. ESCAPE. Two days later, nobody having come for her, she got out by herself: she hit Izek in the face with a brass candlestick in front of six of the Baron's watch, broke his nose, and walked out of the mansion's front door past men who did not know whether to stop her. The watch saw it; he is humiliated. She is back at her refuge, bruised and colder toward the party, who did not come.

Who brings the news depends on where the party is when the visit finds them: at the Blue Water Inn it is URWIN (the innkeeper); at St. Andral's it is FATHER LUCIAN; anywhere else in Vallaki it is a TOWN GUARD (a watchman of the Baron). Whatever the speaker says must read correctly whichever refuge Ireena was in (the inn or the church), so speaker lines are written NEUTRAL about which refuge ("where she sleeps", "her room", "the door") - the Narrator lines, which come first, say which refuge it is.

What the player sees, in order: a Narrator line for the refuge (two versions: inn / church), then the speaker for where the party stands (three versions), then a small menu of what the party can say. Every scene ends the conversation.

## The nodes I need (one line = 1-2 short sentences)

omen_inn: Narrator x1 (a big man stands motionless in the dark street across from the inn, looking up at one shuttered window; the faint red glow of his arm; he has plainly been there for hours)
omen_church: Narrator x1 (the same man at the churchyard gate, one hand on the iron, not coming in; nothing supernatural, just him standing there in the dark looking at the vestry window)
omen_urwin: Urwin x2 (what he has seen: the man has stood there since dusk; nobody dares move him; a warning in his few dry words)
omen_lucian: Father Lucian x2 (the same, in his kind tired voice; a priest who would take her in and knows holy ground does not stop a living man)
omen_guard: Town Guard x2 (the same, in the nervous bureaucratic cheer of the watch: the captain is not ours to order; please do not tell the Baron I said so)
omen_menu: option texts only, one `* ` line: what the party says as the way out (e.g. that they will watch him themselves). Under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we").

taken_inn: Narrator x1 (the party sees Ireena's room at the inn: bed empty, a candle burned down on the floor, the door off one hinge; what a quiet taking leaves behind)
taken_church: Narrator x1 (the vestry bed where she slept: empty, blanket on the floor, the churchyard gate standing open)
taken_urwin: Urwin x3 (he saw Izek take her at the third watch, quietly, as one carries a sleeping child; she did not scream; he did not stop him and is ashamed; he says where: the Baron's mansion, Izek's room off the great hall, the door not locked, Izek sits in front of it)
taken_lucian: Father Lucian x3 (he was at vespers when it happened; the door was not barred; a living man needs no invitation; he blames himself; where she is, the same facts)
taken_guard: Town Guard x3 (Captain Izek carried the red-haired lady to the mansion; nobody asked; orders, he says; where she is, the same facts; please do not tell the Baron)
taken_ismark: Narrator x1 (used only when Ismark (Ireena's adoptive brother, the burgomaster's son, who stayed behind to guard her) was guarding her: he went after them to the mansion gate and the watch turned him back at spear-point; he is out there now, shouting; the party finds him gone from his post)
taken_menu: option texts only, one `* ` line: the party says they are going after her. Under 12 words.

escape_inn: Narrator x1 (the inn's upper room is lit again; a basin of pink water; Ireena sits on the bed with her knuckles bound and does not look up)
escape_church: Narrator x1 (the vestry: Ireena sits very upright on the bed with her hand wrapped in a cloth, a candle burning, and does not look up)
escape_urwin: Urwin x2 (what the whole town now knows: she broke his nose with a candlestick in front of the watch and walked out of the front door; he saw her come back at first light; she asked for nothing)
escape_lucian: Father Lucian x2 (the same, in his voice; he is quietly proud and quietly shaken; she did not come to the church for blessing but for a basin; she asked if the party had come)
escape_guard: Town Guard x2 (the same: six of us stood there and not one moved; the Captain has not been seen since, and nobody is laughing aloud; please do not tell the Baron I said any of this)
escape_menu: option texts only, one `* ` line: the party says they will go and see her. Under 12 words.

That is 29 spoken lines and 4 option texts.

## Canon limits

Do not invent names, places or history beyond what is given: no new named characters (the Baron is only "the Baron"; the innkeepers are Urwin and his wife, who need not appear); no new places beyond the inn, the church, the churchyard gate, the square, the Baron's mansion with Izek's room off the great hall; no new monsters. The Baron's mansion is real and the Baron's men are "the watch". Izek is "the Captain" to the watch and "Izek" to everyone else. He does NOT hurt Ireena; nobody says he did. He took her because he wants to keep her; the speakers do not know why and may guess ("the dolls", "he's been odd about her"). Nobody in these scenes knows she is his sister. Nobody says Strahd's name. In the church scenes, the bones of St. Andral may or may not be back: do not mention the bones. Ireena is not in these scenes (she is only reported). The cost of the party's absence falls on Ireena's trust and Izek's pride, not on anything the speakers say they lost. Moods: a speaker may use [afraid], [sad], [weary], [smile] or [angry], or no mood; the Narrator never has a mood.

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Speaker [mood]: Text` where Speaker is Narrator, Urwin, Father Lucian or Town Guard. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 22 words in total, written to be spoken aloud: NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. Plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names above, each node on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. For the option texts write one `* text` row under that node. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.

## Voice bibles and existing lines (match the register; do not repeat these)

URWIN (speaker `Urwin`). Quiet innkeeper with black hair and black eyes; listens to the room more than he serves it. Secretly one of the Keepers of the Feather, who watch the valley as ravens (do NOT mention this). Few words, all useful. Statements, not questions. Dry, never cruel.
- "Bed's upstairs, meal's on the stove. Questions are free. I might not answer them."
- "Back. Good."
- "Nothing comes in through our windows that we don't let in."
- "Lucian's stripped his altar. Something's gone from the church that shouldn't have."
- "We'll still give you a bed. Danika says it's what you do. We won't sell you anything. I say that's what you do."

FATHER LUCIAN (speaker `Father Lucian`). Careful, kind, tired priest, twenty years at St. Andral's. Plain, warm, a little formal; asks before he tells; keeps catching his sermon instincts and trimming them. Fears he is a coward for not choosing a side. Hope is "the only tool they let me keep".
- "Are you hurt, or hungry, or in trouble? Those are the three reasons people come here now."
- "You held. All night, you held. I've lit a candle for each of you, and one for the windows, which did not."
- "Vargas is a frightened child with a whip. Fiona is a patient woman with a much worse master."
- "Go with God, and come back to us."
- "Gently."

TOWN GUARD (speaker `Town Guard`). Ordinary men with festival ribbons on their spears and orders to report frowning. Bureaucratic cheer over exhaustion. They say the quiet part and then ask you not to repeat it.
- "Halt. Names, business, and how long you mean to stay. And smile, please. It's the law this week."
- "Last week was the Festival of the Returning Swallows. No swallows came. It was still a great success."
- "Same lockup, same key, different people. I'm still here. Somebody has to hold the key."
- "Kolyan's girl? From the village? We heard he'd died. Sorry, miss. The Baron will want to know you're here."

IZEK (he is not in these scenes, but the speakers are describing him). Flat, short, imperatives and threats; never more than two sentences unless he speaks of her. About her he goes quiet and almost gentle, which is worse. Pet phrases: "Not here." "I'm good at waiting."
- "I've seen you. Every night since I was nine years old. I didn't know your name. Now I do."
- "Something took my arm when I was nine and gave me this one. Nothing's frightened me since."

IREENA (she is only reported here, but her trust is the cost). Proud, direct, dry; judges the party by how they treat her father; refuses to be a damsel.
- "I slept through the night. The whole night. I'd forgotten that was a thing people did."
- "Izek comes to the church door at dusk. He doesn't come in. He can't, or he won't. He just stands there."
- "The Martikovs are kind. Urwin sits up all night watching the windows. I've never met a man so interested in birds."

## The Narrator

An old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather. Second person or plain scene description, present tense. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn (irony, dread, dry joke). Ominous, dryly funny, never cruel. Concrete senses over adjectives (a smell, a sound, a temperature). No game terms: never "roll", "check", "DC", "HP", "level". No winks at the player. Here the Narrator is quiet and exact: this is dread, then shame, then a small grim satisfaction.
Samples:
- "The hall smells of beeswax and old smoke. Somebody kept this house beautifully, right up until they didn't."
- "A big man in a watch captain's coat stops dead in the middle of the square. His right arm is wrong: scaled red-black to the shoulder, with claws where the nails should be."
- "He doesn't move until Ireena turns away. Then he watches her go, and goes on watching the place where she was."
- "The Baron's fist went quiet as a struck bell."

body:
Thank you. That was a good first batch. Here is the second and last group, same rules, same format, same canon (plain text only, nodes under `~ name`, `Speaker [mood]: Text`, 1-2 sentences, under about 22 words, ASCII only, no placeholders, finish without sending messages to anyone else). One correction to the first batch for context: in the room, Izek sits INSIDE his own room on the cot, between Ireena and the door; the door is not locked.

## The scenes

The party goes to the Baron's mansion to get Ireena back. She is in Izek's room, off the great hall: a bare soldier's room with a cot, a washstand with a basin, a sword leaning in a corner, a candle, and an open chest of small carved wooden dolls, every one with the same red-haired face (hers; the toymaker carves them for him). The door to the hall is not locked. Izek's right arm is the scaled, clawed, hot one; his left is ordinary. Ireena has not been hurt: he carried her here, put a doll in her lap and sat watching her. She is angry, very controlled, dry, proud; she does not scream and does not beg; she makes the grim joke before anyone can pity her. She will never say Strahd's name. Izek does NOT hurt her; he wants to keep her safe; with her he goes quiet and almost gentle, which is worse. He does not know she is his sister. Neither does she, unless the party tells them (one branch does: the lines for that moment already exist; see below).

The player reaches the room in one of two ways, and some nodes serve both:
- AT NIGHT: Izek is in the room with her. The scene starts by itself when the party comes in.
- BY DAY: Izek is out on the Baron's business (nobody knows where); Ireena is alone in his room with the door shut, not locked, and the watch down the hall who do not ask what the Captain keeps in his room.

How the scene can end (the engine handles the rules; you write the lines):
1. The party threatens him and he gives way: he lets her go.
2. The party tells him the truth (Ireena is his sister) and he believes it: the lines of that moment already exist (listed below); I need the lines AFTER them.
3. The party walks her out by day.
4. The party fights him: before the fight begins, Ireena slips out so she is not caught in it.
Endings 1-3 then share a short tail where Ireena decides: rejoin the party, or be taken back to her refuge.

## Existing lines you must NOT rewrite or repeat (they play already)

Izek: "You're in my room." / "Good. I've wanted to since the gate." / "Kill me? In the Baron's house? Go on, then. Try." / "Liar. You saw the dolls and you made up a story to go with them. Get out of my sight before I forget the Baron likes you."
Truth moment: Izek: "No." Narrator: "He looks at you, and then at nothing, for a very long time. The scaled hand opens and closes. When he speaks again his voice has gone quiet, the way a struck bell goes quiet." Izek: "My sister. My sister had red hair." Izek: "I won't touch her. I won't let anyone touch her. And I won't break any more heads for that fat fool in the sash. I'm done." Ireena [sad]: "I'm sorry. I don't remember you. I wish I did." Izek: "I remember enough for both of us."
Existing at_home Narrator: "Izek sits on his cot in the dark with a doll in his ordinary hand, turning it so the candlelight moves across its painted face. He doesn't get up."
Existing option texts: "We know about the dolls. And about her." / "Izek, we know who the red-haired woman is." / "(Draw steel.) This ends tonight." / "We'll go."

## The nodes I need (one line = 1-2 short sentences)

room_first: Narrator x2 (what the party sees on opening the door: Izek on the cot and Ireena upright in a chair, not tied, a doll face-down on her knee; the open chest; do not repeat the existing at_home narrator line), Izek x2 (AFTER he has said "You're in my room."; he is calm; he explains in his flat way that she is safe here and nobody will take her into the trees; he speaks of her almost gently), Ireena x2 (furious and controlled, dry: he has not touched her, and that is almost worse; she will not be talked about as luggage)
room_again: Izek x1 (the party returns after leaving; short, flat), Ireena x1 (dry)
room_hurt: Ireena x2 (answer to "Are you hurt?": no; he has been very polite; she has been counting the dolls and it is not a comfort)
room_threat_ok: Narrator x1 (he weighs the party and the numbers and his arm stops glowing), Izek x2 (he lets her go; he stays seated; he does not like it; one of the two lines uses his pet phrase "I'm good at waiting" or a close variant)
room_truth_fail: Ireena x1 (said right after Izek calls the party liars: she asks the party to let her speak to him herself)
room_truth_after: Narrator x1 (after "I remember enough for both of us.": he puts the doll down face to the wall and stands out of the doorway), Izek x1 (he tells her to go; he will not follow; a brother's line, flat, no tenderness he can't afford), Ireena x1 (she does not know what to call him; she goes)
room_fight: Ireena x1 (before the fight: she will not be a hostage in a brawl; she says she will be on the stairs; she does not ask them to be careful), Narrator x1 (she goes out past the watch; Izek does not stop her; he is looking at the party)
alone_first: Narrator x1 (by day: Izek's room empty of him; Ireena at the foot of the cot with the doll box open beside her; she has plainly not slept), Ireena x3 (he left at first light; he locked nothing and told nobody; she has not tried the door because the watch in the hall would send word, and she is saving her one try; he comes back at dusk; she does not apologise for being angry at the party for being slow)
alone_again: Ireena x1 (the party comes back by day before getting her out: short, dry)
alone_rescue: Ireena x2 (the party says come on, we are getting you out: practical; she wants her scarf straight and out of the mansion before dusk)
freed: Ireena x3 (shared tail after endings 1-3; written so it reads right after a threat, after the truth, and after a daytime walk-out: thanks, once and not warmly; anger at the Baron's men who did nothing; what she wants to do next)
freed_back: Ireena x1 (the party offers to take her back to where she was sheltering; she accepts but not meekly)
watched: Ireena x2 (the party speaks to her instead of to Izek while he is in the room; she answers low and fast: talk to HIM, not me; he listens to tone not words)

## Option texts (what the party says; each under 12 words, party's voice, "we"; write them as `* text` rows under the node, in this order)

room_first: (1) a question to Ireena asking whether she is hurt; (2) a threat: let her walk out or he will not see another festival
alone_first: (1) tell her they are getting her out now; (2) ask whether he has hurt her; (3) tell her to stay a little longer while they deal with him first
freed: (1) ask her to come with them again; (2) offer to take her back to where she was sheltering

That is 32 spoken lines and 7 option texts.

## Voice reminders

IZEK: flat, short, imperatives; never more than two sentences unless about her. Pet phrases: "Not here." "I'm good at waiting." Moods: [angry], [sad] or none.
- "I've seen you. Every night since I was nine years old. I didn't know your name. Now I do."
- "She's real. I dream her every night. Her face, her hair. When I find her, I'll keep her safe. Nobody will ever take her into the trees again."
- "Then you know I'm not mad. She's real. I'll find her and keep her, and she'll never be cold in the woods again."

IREENA: direct and proud, short sentences, no ornament; asks questions like a magistrate; dry humour with an edge; more formal when grieving; never says "please" to Strahd's name, and does not say his name. Pet phrases: "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly." Moods: [angry], [afraid], [sad], [smile] or none.
- "I am standing right here, and I am not a sack of flour to be handed over a counter."
- "Ismark warned me there'd be men like you. I thought he meant the castle."
- "Good. I was going mad sitting still. Walls didn't keep him out of my father's house; I'd rather take my chances with you."
- "I'd rather he knew. If he's going to look at me like that, I'd rather he knew why."
- "I won't sleep one night in a town that sends its compliments to the castle."

NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences with the second as the turn, concrete senses, never cruel, no game terms. In this scene: tight and quiet, dread and a thread of grim comedy.

## Canon limits

Do not invent names, places or history: no new characters; no name for Izek's lost sister (nobody says it); the Baron is only "the Baron"; the watch is "the watch". Ireena does not fight and does not pick up anything to fight with in these scenes (she is kept out of fights). Izek never hurts her and no line says he did. Nobody says Strahd's name. No game terms. The consequence for waiting too long is in her coldness and his pride, not in injury.

Format reminder: one line per row, `Speaker [mood]: Text`; speakers are Narrator, Izek, Ireena. Group under `~ node_name` in the order given. Option texts as `* text` rows under their node. No commentary.

* Let us take you back to where you were sheltering.

~ freed_back
Ireena: Very well, we'll go back for tonight. At least there they ask my name before they shut the door.

~ watched
Ireena [afraid]: Don't talk to me while he's watching your hands. Speak to him, and keep your voice flat.
Ireena: He isn't listening to the words. He's waiting for an excuse to reach for that sword in the corner.

body:
Thank you, both batches were useful. One small last group, same rules and format (plain text only, nodes under `~ name`, `Speaker [mood]: Text`, 1-2 sentences, under about 22 words, ASCII only, no placeholders, finish without sending messages to anyone else).

## The scene

After Ireena has been taken to Izek's room and has got away from him (she got out alone and broke his nose with a candlestick in front of the watch; or the party walked her out by day; or the party made him let her go with a threat), the party can find Izek again at night in his room off the great hall at the Baron's mansion: the same bare room, the cot, the washstand, the sword in the corner, the open chest of red-haired wooden dolls. He is alone now. Ireena is not there. He does not know she is his sister, and nobody in this scene says so. He is not repentant: he still thinks he was keeping her safe, and he still wants her. But the thing that made him sure of himself has gone.

Two variants, chosen by how it ended:
- AFTER_ESCAPE: she got out alone and broke his nose in front of six of the Baron's watch. He is humiliated. His nose is swollen and bruised dark; he has splinted it with a strip of tin or a folded cloth. He sits on the cot with a doll in his ordinary (left) hand and does not look up when the party comes in. He is quiet, flat and, for him, almost honest. He admits (once, in his own flat way) that she walked past him and he did not stop her, and that he does not know why.
- AFTER_PARTY: the party walked her out by day, or forced him to let her go. He is angry but cold, not loud: he counts what was taken out of his room (he does not say "mine" about a person: he says "she"), and he repeats that he is good at waiting.

The first line the player hears is a Narrator line; Izek speaks next; then the conversation goes on into the menu that already exists (a menu where the party may threaten him, tell him the truth if they know it, draw steel, or go). So these lines only OPEN the scene. Do not write the menu.

## Existing lines you must not repeat

Izek: "You're in my room." / "Good. I've wanted to since the gate." / "Then you know I'm not mad. She's real. I'll find her and keep her, and she'll never be cold in the woods again." / "He said no. In front of everyone. I'll wait. I'm good at waiting." / "The Baron's happy. That makes one of us."
In the last batch he also said: "She stays here where the walls are thick and the watch knows my door. Nobody takes her back into the trees while I'm breathing." and "I'm good at waiting. A man with one room and a long memory doesn't have to hurry." (so do not use that last phrase again in the party variant; find another way to say he will wait).

## The nodes I need

after_hold_escaped: Narrator x1 (what the party sees: the nose, the tin splint or cloth, the doll in his left hand, the chest of dolls shut now, perhaps the brass candlestick that broke his nose standing back on the washstand), Izek x2 (flat; the watch saw; nobody laughed to his face, which is worse; she walked past him and he did not stop her and he does not know why)
after_hold_party: Narrator x1 (the same room with an empty chair set square in the middle, the doll on the cot, the chest shut), Izek x2 (cold; she is gone out of his room and he has counted the dolls twice; he does not threaten; he says he will wait without using the phrase "good at waiting" again)

That is 6 lines.

## Voice reminders

IZEK: flat, short, imperatives; never more than two sentences unless about her; about her he goes quiet and almost gentle, which is worse. Moods: [angry], [sad] or none.
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, the second a turn; concrete senses; never cruel; no game terms.

## Canon limits

No new characters, places or history. Nobody says Ireena's name in Izek's mouth unless it is "she"; Izek may say "her". Nobody says Strahd's name. Do not name Izek's lost sister. He does not hurt anyone in this scene.

Format reminder: one line per row, `Speaker [mood]: Text`; speakers are Narrator and Izek. Group under `~ node_name` in the order given. No commentary.

~ after_hold_escaped
Narrator: Izek sits by the shut chest with a doll in his left hand and a tin splint across his blackened nose. The bent brass candlestick stands washed upon the basin.
Izek [angry]: Six of the watch saw it, and not one of them dared laugh to my face. That's worse.
Izek: She walked right past me with my blood on her cuff, and I didn't lift a hand. I don't know why.

~ after_hold_party
Narrator: An empty chair sits square in the middle of the bare room, the chest shut tight beside the washstand. On the cot, a single red-haired doll lies beside his knee.
Izek [angry]: She's gone out of this room, and I've counted the box twice to be sure what's left. The room's cold again.
Izek: It doesn't matter where you hide her. The town has walls, and I have all the nights there are.
